title: Multimodal digital biomarker for asthma: complementary roles of vocal, clinical and demographic factors

abstract: Asthma affects over 260 million people worldwide, yet diagnosis remains dependent on spirometry and specialist assessment, limiting accessibility in primary care and low-resource settings. Vocal biomarkers offer a promising non-invasive alternative, but prior studies have largely focused on acoustic features without integrating clinical context. We present a multimodal Mixture-of-Experts framework for asthma identification that adaptively combines acoustic embeddings from sustained vowel phonation and reading passage tasks with structured clinical and demographic data. The model was evaluated on a matched cohort of 1218 self-reported asthma cases and healthy controls from the Colive Voice study. The multimodal model achieved an AUROC of 0.83 and Brier score of 0.18, outperforming unimodal approaches. Exploratory analysis of the gating mechanism in asthma cases showed that greater respiratory symptom burden was associated with increased weighting of reading-passage modality and reduced weighting of sustained-vowel phonation modality. These findings support the feasibility of voice-based identification of self-reported asthma; however, independent prospective validation remains necessary before clinical use.

abstract: [Journal of thoracic oncology : official publication of the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer] Artificial intelligence (AI) is starting to transform pathology by enhancing diagnostic accuracy, prognostication, and therapeutic prediction through advanced computational analysis of histopathological images. This review explores key AI methodologies and their applications in lung cancer diagnostics. Supervised learning dominates current clinical AI tools, relying on annotated whole-slide images (WSIs) for tasks like tumor subtyping, quantitation of tissue-based parameters, prediction of driver alterations (e.g. EGFR and KRAS mutations, ALK rearrangement), and assessment of tumor microenvironment (TME) features. Meanwhile, weakly supervised and self-supervised learning (SSL) methods, such as multiple instance learning (MIL) and contrastive learning, reduce dependency on labor-intensive annotations and uncover novel prognostic morphologic patterns. AI demonstrates strong performance in predicting therapeutic responses, including immune checkpoint inhibitor efficacy and pathologic response to neoadjuvant therapy, while emerging techniques like spatial transcriptomics and multiplex immunofluorescence further leverage AI to decode complex spatial biology and generate novel biomarkers. Despite much progress, major challenges persist in validation, reliability, interpretability, regulatory approval, ethics and data privacy standards, cost and reimbursement, equity, and integration into clinical workflows. Adoption requires scalable digital pathology infrastructure, interdisciplinary collaboration, and suitable reimbursement frameworks. Regulatory efforts aim to address ethical and safety concerns, but global harmonization remains incomplete. We also consider the professional consequences of adoption, including cognitive deskilling, workforce displacement, and the conditions under which pathologist oversight remains meaningful rather than nominal, and argue that liability should follow the reality of control. As AI evolves, particularly with foundation models and large language models (LLMs), thoracic pathology stands to benefit from substantially extended diagnostic and predictive capabilities, pending resolution of implementation barriers.
zh_abstract: 【Journal of thoracic oncology：国际肺癌研究协会官方出版物】人工智能（AI）正开始通过先进的计算分析组织病理学图像来增强诊断准确性、预后判断和治疗预测，从而改变病理学。本综述探讨关键AI方法学及其在肺癌诊断中的应用。监督学习在当前的临床AI工具中占主导地位，依赖标注的全切片图像（WSIs）完成肿瘤亚型分型、组织基参数定量、驱动基因改变预测（如EGFR和KRAS突变、ALK重排）以及肿瘤微环境（TME）特征评估等任务。与此同时，弱监督和自监督学习（SSL）方法，如多实例学习（MIL）和对比学习，减少了对劳动密集型标注的依赖，并揭示了新的预后形态学模式。AI在预测治疗反应方面表现出强大性能，包括免疫检查点抑制剂疗效和新辅助治疗病理学反应，而空间转录组学和多路免疫荧光等新兴技术进一步利用AI解码复杂空间生物学并生成新型生物标志物。尽管取得很大进展，但在验证、可靠性、可解释性、监管批准、伦理和数据隐私标准、成本与报销、公平性以及整合到临床工作流程方面仍存在重大挑战。采用需要可扩展的数字病理基础设施、跨学科合作和合适的报销框架。监管努力旨在解决伦理和安全问题，但全球协调仍不完整。我们还考虑了采用带来的职业后果，包括认知去技能化、劳动力替代，以及病理学家监督在何种条件下仍具有实质意义而非名义上的意义，并主张责任应随控制权的现实而定。随着AI发展，尤其是基础模型和大语言模型（LLMs），胸部病理学有望获得大幅扩展的诊断和预测能力，前提是实施障碍得到解决。

title: Large Language Model-Assisted Cleaning of Report-Derived Labels in a Large-Scale Chest CT Dataset.

abstract: [Journal of medical systems] To evaluate whether large language model (LLM)-assisted label cleaning can identify label-report discordance in CT-RATE, a large-scale public chest CT dataset. After report-level deduplication, 24,446 unique radiology reports from 20,209 unique patients were identified. Twelve reports were excluded from the primary GPT-5.4 analysis because of persistent content-safety filtering or unparsable output, leaving 24,434 reports and 439,812 label instances across 18 abnormality categories. GPT-5.4-derived binary labels were generated from report text using structured outputs and compared with the original CT-RATE labels. Discordant instances were adjudicated by radiologists. In addition, 100 randomly sampled reports were manually annotated as a development set to compare the original CT-RATE labels, individual LLM-derived labels, and three-LLM majority-vote labels against radiologist-annotated reference labels. These label sources were then evaluated against a prespecified, stratified confirmatory set of 250 reports independently annotated by two blinded radiologists, and run-to-run consistency was assessed by repeated runs. Overall agreement between GPT-5.4-derived and CT-RATE labels was 96.4%, with a Cohen's κ of 0.884. Lymphadenopathy showed the lowest agreement and κ. In the confirmatory set (pre-consensus inter-reader κ = 0.936), the majority vote achieved an unweighted label-macro-averaged F1 score of 95.6% and κ of 0.940, compared with 90.8% and 0.879 for the original labels (paired F1 difference, + 4.8 points; 95% CI, 3.6-6.2), and each individual LLM also outperformed the original labels. The instance-level flip rate across three repeated runs was 1.02% for the majority vote. LLM-assisted label cleaning identified substantial label-report discordance in CT-RATE, particularly for lymphadenopathy, and may provide a scalable approach to quality improvement of public imaging datasets. The refined report-aligned labels and associated code will be made publicly available upon acceptance. Because all labels were derived from report text, they reflect report alignment rather than image-level truth.
zh_abstract: [Journal of medical systems] 评估大语言模型（LLM）辅助的标签清洗是否能够识别CT-RATE这一大规模公共胸部CT数据集中的标签-报告不一致。报告层面去重后，识别出来自20,209名唯一患者的24,446份唯一放射学报告。12份报告因持续的内容安全过滤或输出无法解析而被排除在主要GPT-5.4分析之外，剩余24,434份报告和跨18个异常类别的439,812个标签实例。使用结构化输出从报告文本生成GPT-5.4衍生的二分类标签，并与原始CT-RATE标签比较。不一致实例由放射科医师裁定。此外，随机抽取100份报告进行人工标注作为开发集，以将原始CT-RATE标签、单个LLM衍生标签和三个LLM多数投票标签与放射科医师标注的参考标签进行比较。随后，在由两名盲法放射科医师独立标注的、预先指定的分层确认集（250份报告）中评估这些标签来源，并通过重复运行评估运行间一致性。GPT-5.4衍生标签与CT-RATE标签的总体一致率为96.4%，Cohen's κ为0.884。淋巴结病的一致率和κ最低。在确认集中（共识前读者间κ = 0.936），多数投票达到未加权的标签宏平均F1分数95.6%和κ 0.940，而原始标签为90.8%和0.879（配对F1差异，+4.8分；95% CI，3.6-6.2），并且每个单独LLM也优于原始标签。多数投票在三次重复运行中的实例级翻转率为1.02%。LLM辅助标签清洗在CT-RATE中识别出大量标签-报告不一致，尤其是淋巴结病，并可能为公共影像数据集的质量改进提供可扩展的方法。经改进的与报告对齐的标签及相关代码将在接收后公开。由于所有标签均源自报告文本，它们反映的是与报告的对齐，而非图像层面的真实标签。

title: An open long non-coding RNA foundation model for generalizable prediction
zh_title: 开源长非编码RNA基础模型LncRFM
summary: 发布开源lncRNA基础模型LncRFM，配套预训练数据LncCorpus与评测套件LncBench。
key_points: 针对千碱基级lncRNA长程结构建模
采用混合双向状态空间编码器

reason: 开源专用基础模型并配数据/基准，预印本证据有限
abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) play essential roles in transcriptional regulation and chromatin organization, yet predicting their functional properties from sequence remains challenging because informative signals span both local motifs and long-range base pairing across kilobase-scale transcripts. Current RNA foundation models are restricted to short sequences and existing lncRNA prediction models narrowly focus on isolated tasks, leaving a dedicated foundation model notably absent. Here we present LncRFM, a dedicated lncRNA foundation model, supported by the LncCorpus pretraining data and the LncBench evaluation suite, which stand for a systematic framework to decode lncRNAs. For foundation model pretraining, we develop a hybrid bidirectional state-space encoder trained with a structure-guided masking strategy to effectively capture both local sequence patterns and long-range contexts. For pretraining data, we contribute over 9.6 million lncRNA sequences to assemble LncCorpus, a pretraining corpus of 24.7 million sequences. For benchmarking evaluation, we construct a comprehensive benchmark, LncBench, comprising 15 datasets and totaling over 1,010,000 sequences across 10 prediction tasks: six core lncRNA functional and annotation tasks and four structural and regulatory RNA assay tasks. Evaluated against seven RNA foundation models under a unified frozen-encoder protocol, our LncRFM achieves the state-of-the-art primary-metric scores on 11 of the 13 datasets that allow downstream adaptation. On two external generalization benchmarks evaluated without further adaptation, LncRFM matches the best structure-specialized baseline in F1 (0.141) and achieves the highest AUROC (0.962) on lncRNA contact prediction, while maintaining competitive cross-species coding-potential transfer (F1 of 0.374) under severe multi-kingdom domain shift. To benefit the scientific community, we make all datasets, source code, and pretrained models publicly available.
zh_abstract: 长非编码RNA（lncRNA）在转录调控和染色质组织中发挥重要作用，但仅从序列预测其功能特性仍具挑战性，因为信息信号既跨越局部基序，也跨越千碱基级转录本中的长程碱基配对。当前的RNA基础模型局限于短序列，现有lncRNA预测模型则狭隘地聚焦于孤立任务，因此明显缺乏专门的基礎模型。在此，我们提出LncRFM，一个专门的lncRNA基础模型，并由LncCorpus预训练数据和LncBench评估套件支持，二者构成解码lncRNA的系统性框架。对于基础模型预训练，我们开发了一种混合双向状态空间编码器，采用结构引导的掩码策略训练，以有效捕获局部序列模式和长程上下文。对于预训练数据，我们贡献了超过960万条lncRNA序列，以组装LncCorpus——一个包含2,470万条序列的预训练语料库。对于基准评估，我们构建了一个综合基准LncBench，包含15个数据集，总计超过1,010,000条序列，覆盖10项预测任务：六项核心lncRNA功能与注释任务，以及四项结构与调控RNA实验任务。在统一的冻结编码器协议下，与七个RNA基础模型进行评估，我们的LncRFM在允许下游适配的13个数据集中的11个上取得最先进的主要指标分数。在两个无需进一步适配即评估的外部泛化基准上，LncRFM在lncRNA接触预测中与最佳结构专用基线在F1（0.141）上持平，并取得最高AUROC（0.962），同时在严重的多界域偏移下保持有竞争力的跨物种编码潜力迁移（F1为0.374）。为造福科学界，我们公开所有数据集、源代码和预训练模型。

abstract: [Current problems in pediatric and adolescent health care] Adolescent mental health remains a topic of concern in the United States and worldwide. The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the youth mental health crisis, which began nearly a decade earlier. The ongoing shortage of mental health professionals, including therapists and child and adolescent psychiatrists, means many adolescents who require mental health treatment do not receive it. The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) technology has demonstrated promise in the field of adolescent mental health, including in screening, detection and risk prediction, intervention and treatment, clinical decision support and workflow augmentation, and in the training of future mental health professionals. However, the study of AI tools in the mental health space remains in its infancy, and most are not yet ready for routine use in clinical practice. Furthermore, the potential risks of AI and its use in adolescent mental health treatment are significant and must be addressed prior to widespread use. Health care professionals, adolescents, and their caregivers need to develop AI literacy to use the technology safely and responsibly. abstract: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] Multi-omics integration amalgamates genomic, transcriptomic, epigenomic, and proteomic layers to provide a systems-level portrait of multifaceted diseases such as cancer. However, its practical application faces constraints posed by challenges including elevated dimensionality, diverse data types, and prevalent missing values. This review delivers a structured summary of recent advances in machine-learning-driven integration of multi-omics datasets, with a specific emphasis on the potential of this field for translational cancer research. First, we discuss the importance of multi-omics integration. Next, we provide an overview of key machine learning methodologies, including high-dimensional variable selection techniques (e.g., knockoff filters for controlling the false discovery rate), deep learning models (for survival prediction and classification), and generative models (e.g., diffusion models and variational autoencoders for data augmentation and missing data imputation). These approaches demonstrate high accuracy in cancer subtype classification, biomarker discovery, prognosis evaluation, and personalized therapy. For example, they achieve over 85% accuracy in triple-negative breast cancer subtype analysis. We also cover the contributions of single-cell multi-omics technologies (e.g., SHARE-seq and SNARE-seq) and emerging databases (e.g., scImmOmics and scCancerExplorer) to enhancing data resolution. While challenges remain in terms of interpretability and computational efficiency, integrating explainable AI and multimodal learning shows promise in accelerating clinical translation. This review seeks to equip researchers with a systematic methodological roadmap and demonstrate its practical utility in precision medicine via exemplar case studies.

abstract: [Biomarker research] Although immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed breast cancer treatment, predicting durable clinical benefit remains challenging. Current biomarkers, primarily derived from tumor tissue or peripheral blood, do not directly capture the adaptive immune response at its site of initiation. Tumor-draining lymph nodes (TDLNs) are not passive conduits for metastasis but dynamic immunological hubs where anti-tumor T cell priming and immune evasion converge. In this review, we critically examine the nascent intersection of TDLN immunobiology, high-resolution multi-omics, and artificial intelligence (AI) to evaluate TDLN-derived features as candidate next-generation biomarkers for immunotherapy. We synthesize the complex cellular and molecular architecture of the breast cancer TDLN, including T cell exhaustion, B cell-mediated immunity, and stromal crosstalk, before evaluating the state-of-the-art single-cell and spatial technologies capable of decoding this microenvironment. We assess the application of AI and foundation models in this domain, identifying a major methodological gap: while AI frameworks are increasingly mature for primary tumors, their application to TDLNs remains unvalidated and limited by a severe scarcity of annotated multi-omics datasets. Furthermore, we address pivotal translational considerations, including the immunological implications of axillary surgery in the ICI era. We emphasize that no TDLN-derived biomarker has yet undergone prospective validation as a predictive biomarker for immunotherapy in breast cancer, and that retrospective analyses of trial specimens must account for the timing of tissue acquisition relative to systemic therapy. Finally, we chart immediate research priorities, including establishing TDLN reference atlases and developing clinically feasible specimen collection pathways for biomarker validation. This review provides a conceptual framework and translational roadmap to assess whether TDLN-derived features can complement existing tumor-centric metrics in guiding immunotherapy decisions.

abstract: Microbiome data analysis demands customized workflows tailored to specific biological questions, sequencing modalities, and data properties. However, constructing and executing these workflows requires navigating heterogeneous software dependencies, reference databases, and multi-step parameter tuning. Here, we present MicroBioAgent, an autonomous, domain-specific agent framework that translates high-level biological queries into executable, study-specific pipelines across 16S rRNA amplicon, reference-based shotgun, and de novo assembly-based metagenomics. Rather than relying on static pipeline templates, MicroBioAgent employs a closed-loop execution architecture: it dynamically selects and runs bioinformatics tools within user-controlled environments while iteratively inspecting intermediate outputs to adapt downstream analytical decisions. Furthermore, to address the long-running nature of metagenomic computation, we introduce an asynchronous background task-management mechanism that reduces LLM token consumption by over 50% while enabling real-time plan adjustment and automated workflow resumption. We systematically evaluated MicroBioAgent across three benchmarks of increasing complexity: (1) paired amplicon and shotgun profiling of tomato rhizosphere microbiomes, (2) taxonomic and functional profiling coupled with machine-learning classification in a colorectal cancer cohort, and (3) de novo metagenomic assembly, metagenome-assembled genome (MAG) binning, and metabolic pathway reconstruction in a polyethylene degradation study. Across all benchmarks, MicroBioAgent faithfully recapitulated the primary biological findings of the original studies, exhibiting high analytical concordance despite expected tool- and database-dependent variations. In systematic robustness evaluations across 27 independent runs spanning three backbone large language models and three prompt-complexity tiers, MicroBioAgent achieved a 98.8% task completion rate and yielded highly reproducible diversity and differential-abundance estimates. MicroBioAgent establishes a scalable, adaptive paradigm for end-to-end computational microbiome research.

abstract: [Systematic reviews] Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) imposes a substantial burden on patients and healthcare systems. Although traditional risk assessment tools exist, machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) may offer improved prediction. This systematic review aims to evaluate the performance of ML and DL algorithms for predicting AECOPD risk. This review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library and Web of Science were systematically searched from 1 January 2021 to 6 May 2026. Studies that developed or validated ML and DL models for predicting AECOPD risk were included. Methodological quality, risk of bias and applicability were assessed using the PROBAST + AI, and reporting quality was assessed using the TRIPOD + AI. Because of substantial heterogeneity, we synthesised model performance descriptively. Thirteen studies were included, of which only two performed external validation. Overall, reported AUC values ranged widely from 0.661 to 0.9721. By outcome type, AUC values for AECOPD risk prediction ranged from 0.668 to 0.9721, whereas those for AECOPD‑related hospitalisation ranged from 0.661 to 0.885. Similarly, by prediction windows, short‑term prediction achieved AUCs of 0.668‑0.972, compared with 0.661‑0.884 for long‑term prediction. However, PROBAST + AI revealed high methodological quality concerns and risk of bias in all 13 studies, and TRIPOD + AI showed suboptimal reporting transparency with an overall completeness rate of 54.3%. Limited evidence indicates that models for any AECOPD may outperform those for hospitalisation, and that models with shorter prediction windows may show higher AUCs, although this association could be confounded by small sample sizes and potential patient-level leakage. These findings provide valuable direction for future model development and validation, although the current evidence base is constrained by methodological quality concerns, risk of bias and suboptimal reporting transparency. abstract: [Frontiers in public health] The evolution of medical epistemology from the unassailable authority of eminence to the empirical rigour of evidence has prepared the healthcare system for its most profound transformation yet, intelligence-based medicine. Driven by the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), this emerging era offers unprecedented capabilities to process complex health data and personalise patient care within high-stakes environments like emergency departments. However, this paradigm shift simultaneously introduces a critical risk of modernised, digital dogma, manifesting as algorithmic paternalism. If AI systems are deployed without rigorous oversight, they threaten to silently amplify historical biases, diagnostic inaccuracies, and outdated clinical heuristics, trading the unquestioned authority of historical figures for the presumed infallibility of machines. To safeguard care in emergency departments, AI must not operate unchecked. Adapting existing Learning Health System frameworks offers a pragmatic solution to govern AI integration. By embedding these computational technologies within continuous, self-correcting clinical ecosystems, departments can enforce robust data hygiene and rigorously audit data provenance. An essential component of this approach is separating objective safety surveillance and adverse event reporting from the algorithm's internal learning mechanisms to detect epistemic drift and automation bias. Ultimately, the successful and safe integration of intelligence-based medicine depends on an unwavering commitment to transparent governance. When computational power is harnessed as a regulated, transparent tool within an LHS, AI can actively dismantle entrenched clinical dogma, ensuring future care is anchored in dynamic, validated evidence rather than perpetuating the medical errors propagated by eminence from the past.

abstract: [bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology] Timecourse single-cell RNA (scRNA) datasets have become indispensable biological tools for studying and uncovering the underlying regulatory processes driving continuous cell-state transitions such as the epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition. However, these highly fluid, non-linear gene program dynamics remain difficult to disentangle. While deep neural network models can effectively map complex topologies, they are biological black boxes, lacking the gene-level interpretability required by experimental practitioners. Here, we introduce scCont, a fully unsupervised contrastive learning framework for extracting interpretable functional transition units from scRNA-seq data. Rather than relying on explicit temporal labels or clustering priors, scCont uses an unsupervised k-nearest neighbors approach to project local transcriptomic neighborhoods into a low-dimensional embedding. During post-training analysis, scCont employs Shapley network attribution to determine gene-latent relationships, mapping latent dimensions directly into functional gene programs. We quantitatively and qualitatively validate this representation by demonstrating that scCont captures biologically interpretable dynamics more effectively than baseline methods such as LDVAE. Evaluated across 13 diverse EMT timecourse datasets and four simulated datasets, scCont exposes interpretable functional dynamics and effectively maps context-dependent functional groups, helping to bridge the gap between deep learning representation and translational biological utility. scCont is an open source software available on GitHub ( https://github.com/nramani611/scCont ).

abstract: [Frontiers in microbiology] Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in Staphylococcus aureus is a growing clinical threat, and machine learning (ML) offers a scalable approach to identifying allele-level resistance determinants. Using a dataset of 300 clinical isolates, we trained and compared seven ML models - LSTM, CNN, Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), Decision Tree, XGBoost, Logistic Regression, and Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) - to predict resistance across six clinically important antibiotics from allele, locus-tag, and EggNOG-annotation features. Training-set class imbalance was corrected with SMOTE and all seven models were retrained under one identical pipeline. XGBoost achieved the strongest overall test-set performance (accuracy 95%, ROC AUC 0.9745, F1-score 0.9474), closely matched by Decision Tree (accuracy 95%, F1-score 0.9520). Both outperformed the deep-learning architectures (LSTM, CNN, MLP), which showed pronounced overfitting after class-imbalance correction. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis identified "cat__allele_Cluster_1015_Allele_8" as the most influential feature; this association is hypothesis-generating and reflects statistical importance within this dataset, not a confirmed causal or biological mechanism. The genomic feature set was selected once, on the full isolate collection, by a prior SVM-RFE pipeline before the present train/test split, and no external, temporal, or multi-center validation dataset was used. Reported performance should therefore be read as an upper-bound, best-case estimate rather than a validated benchmark. These findings support ML, and ensemble methods such as XGBoost and Decision Tree in particular, as candidate components of future AMR surveillance and diagnostic pipelines, pending external and prospective validation.

abstract: [Proceedings of the ... International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications. International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications] Immunohistochemistry (IHC) staining is frequently used to resolve diagnostically ambiguous prostate cancer biopsy findings on hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained tissue. However, PIN-4 IHC is typically performed on adjacent tissue sections, limiting direct spatial comparison between the H&E morphology that indicated the need for IHC and the corresponding immunophenotypic signal. A paired, registered H&E/PIN-4 dataset was constructed from routine clinical prostate biopsy whole-slide images (WSIs), and a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) was trained to synthesize PIN-4 staining patterns directly from native H&E image patches. The final dataset comprised 172 paired WSIs from 93 patients and 27,298 registered 1024 × 1024 patch pairs, spanning adenocarcinoma-positive and benign cases with representation across age, race, and ethnicity groups. The model was evaluated on an independent held-out test set of 1,814 patch pairs from 17 WSIs, achieving a mean peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of 21.88 dB, structural similarity index measure (SSIM) of 0.667, Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) of 0.684, and learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS) of 0.417. Qualitative review by a board-certified pathologist demonstrated that generated images captured diagnostically relevant PIN-4 staining patterns, including AMACR/racemase expression and basal-cell-associated staining, while preserving spatial correspondence with the source H&E morphology. Synthesis quality varied across morphologically complex regions, including high-grade carcinoma and intraductal carcinoma. These results support the feasibility of supervised computational PIN-4 staining from routinely acquired brightfield H&E prostate biopsy images. The approach enables direct interpretation of predicted PIN-4 marker patterns in the context of the source prostate H&E architecture, addressing a current spatial limitation of conventional adjacent-section IHC.

abstract: [Healthcare informatics research] This study quantitatively evaluated the accuracy and clinical reliability of EzOrtho, deep learning software designed to identify anatomical landmarks automatically for orthodontic diagnosis. Real-world clinical data were used to assess its applicability in practice. We analyzed 23 lateral cephalometric radiographs. EzOrtho automatically identified 36 anatomical landmarks per radiograph, yielding 828 data points for comparison with ground truth established by experienced orthodontists using a standardized annotation protocol. Accuracy was quantified using mean radial error (MRE), and clinical reliability was assessed using the successful detection rate (SDR), defined as the percentage of all points within the clinically acceptable threshold of 2.0 mm. The overall MRE was 0.78 mm, and the SDR at the 2.0 mm threshold was 86%. Although most landmarks were detected precisely, the landmark-specific analysis identified higher error rates at a few points in anatomically complex regions, indicating areas for improvement. The findings suggest that EzOrtho may offer clinical utility and reliability for automatic cephalometric landmark detection using real clinical data. Its performance indicates the potential to improve efficiency and consistency relative to manual tracing. However, the study's limitations, including its small sample size, mean that these results remain preliminary. Further validation is needed to establish its role as a decision-support tool in orthodontic practice.
